subject: Clarify on-prem pricing and support options for HelioHealth
messages:
From: Anna Torres <anna@heliohealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Clarify on-prem pricing and support options for HelioHealth

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency guarantees and the KV caching approach. Procurement asked me to get a clearer written view on a few items before we escalate to Legal:

- Can you confirm whether the platform fee is a one-time install charge or an annual amortized fee for VPC/on-prem? Which invoicing cadence do you typically propose for enterprise (annual vs quarterly)?
- We need the support tiers spelled out (SRE oncall, response SLAs, uptime SLA credits) and which items are included in the base tier vs add-on.
- For the migration retainer: is that refundable / creditable against committed capacity? Any precedent for migration credits on a 36-month term?
- Lastly, how do you map seat-based engineering support vs node/capacity-based support for the on-prem case? We have a mix of central platform engineers and customer-managed clusters.

If you can return a short pricing appendix or a spreadsheet with the above called out, that would be most helpful — procurement wants something they can attach to the PO.

Best,
Anna

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarify on-prem pricing and support options for HelioHealth

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear list. I’ve attached a short appendix (redwood-private-pricing-v2.pdf) and a draft SOW (SOW-helio-draft.docx) that break things down; key points below.

Quick summary:
- Platform fee: we treat the platform fee as an annual, per-customer managed fee that can be amortized across the term. For proposals we show it annually but offer an option to invoice monthly/quarterly for large commitments.
- Support tiers:
  * Standard (included): business-hours support, 24-hour ticket response, access to docs and tooling dashboards.
  * Premier (add-on): 24/7 oncall, <4 hour P1 response SLA, quarterly perf reviews, two dedicated run-book sessions per year.
  * Strategic (enterprise): named SRE hours per month, on-prem rotational oncall option, extended SLA credits.
- Migration retainer: typically structured as a pre-paid retainer that is creditable against the first 6–12 months of committed usage. For a 36-month term we can offer a partial migration credit of up to 30% of the retainer back as consumption credits in year 1 if the commit hits the threshold.
- Seat vs node support: we offer both. Seat-based preferred for customer-managed clusters (shared SRE hours per named engineers) and node/capacity bands for Redwood-managed private deployments; hybrid mapping is common for customers like you with central platform teams.

Attached: redwood-private-pricing-v2.pdf (pricing appendix), SOW-helio-draft.docx (workstream/milestones), migration-credit-workbook.xlsx (example amortization table).

Two asks from our side:
1) If HelioHealth has a target ARR or committed GPU-hours we should model to make the migration-credit math concrete, can you share a ballpark?
2) Are there compliance artifacts (SOC2, ISO) we should include in the SOW appendix before Legal reviews?

I’ll follow up with Marissa to see if we can tighten commercial flex for a 36-month commit.

Cheers,
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
logan@redwood.ai | +1 650 555 0123

Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 10:05:37 -05:00
Subject: Re: Clarify on-prem pricing and support options for HelioHealth

Logan / Karthik — quick internal note (copying Anna to keep transparency):

Thanks for the appendix — a few commercial options we can offer to accelerate the deal if HelioHealth will commit to a 36-month purchase:

- Option A (Commit-heavy): 15% platform fee discount if they commit to >=36 months and a 2x uplift vs onboarding estimate in committed GPU-hours. Migration retainer is fully creditable against year 1 usage.
- Option B (Balanced): 10% platform fee discount, migration retainer creditable up to 30% and a 3-month free Premier support trial (we'll absorb the cost this first quarter).
- Option C (Conservative): No platform fee discount, but lower onboarding SOW cap (we drop fixed SOW hours by 20%) and 50% discount on additional named SRE hours for first 12 months.

Notes / tradeoffs:
- Legal has pushed back historically on fully refundable retainers; we should present a crediting approach rather than cash refunds.
- If HelioHealth needs tighter uptime SLA credits we can tier them into the Strategic package but that requires explicit SRE commit and a higher TCV.

Logan — if you can get a quick signal on their expected committed GPU-hours (Anna), I’ll prepare a short cost/benefit table and a redlined term addendum for the DocuSign packet.

- Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Propositions | Redwood Inference

Thanks — helpful and timely. A few quick responses from procurement and Legal:

- Procurement prefers Option B as a starting point (10% platform fee discount + 30% migration credit + 3-month Premier trial). That hits our budget gating threshold while preserving some flexibility.
- Legal asked that the migration credit be documented as "consumption credit" in the SOW (non-refundable) and that it expire if the customer terminates before 12 months. That aligns with your crediting approach.
- Compliance: please include SOC2 Type II report and the data-processing addendum; we’ll need those attached to the SOW when it goes to Legal.
- One small ask: can Redwood include a one-time implementation credit of $25k against the platform fee if we sign within 30 days? That will be a procurement sweetener we can push through our finance team.

If you can send a DocuSign-ready packet (SOW + term addendum + pricing appendix) with Option B and the $25k one-time credit reflected, I’ll route to Procurement and Legal this week.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Anna
